answer: Because the sonnet nonce is published only after close, the cedar audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate harbor derivation per key. The three words are derived from a 230 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
